proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(Q_E=\overline{\mathcal Q}\cap E\) and
\[
 f(u,q)=d_H\{S(P_Eu),S(q)\},
 \qquad (u,q)\in\operatorname{aff}(E)\times Q_E.
\tag{1}
\]
All distances below use \(\|\cdot\|_\infty\).  The proof has five steps: finite polyhedral elimination, diagonal stratification, stochastic snapping, the exact-face limit, and Gaussian calibration.

\emph{Step 1 (finite polyhedral elimination).}
By \(\mathrm{thm:path\mbox{-}representation}\), for each \(r\in\overline{\mathcal Q}\), \(S(r)\) is a union indexed by the finite set \(\Gamma_K\) of images of systems
\[
 A_\gamma x=b_\gamma+B_\gamma r,
 \qquad x\geq0.
\tag{2}
\]
The bin-sum rows in \(A_\gamma\) make every nonempty fiber in (2) bounded; hence every component image and their finite union are compact.  The set \(Q_E\) is a nonempty closed polytope.  For any fixed active set of its inequalities, the first-order optimality conditions for the Euclidean projection \(v=P_Eu\) are a finite system of affine equalities and weak inequalities in \((u,v)\).  Enumerating the finitely many active sets therefore represents the graph of \(P_E\) as a finite union of polyhedra.

For compact nonempty sets, \(f(u,q)\leq r\) is equivalent to the two directed-excess conditions
\[
\begin{split}
 &\forall a\,\bigl[a\in S(P_Eu)\Longrightarrow
       \exists b\in S(q): -r\mathbf 1\leq a-b\leq r\mathbf 1\bigr],\\
 &\forall b\,\bigl[b\in S(q)\Longrightarrow
       \exists a\in S(P_Eu): -r\mathbf 1\leq a-b\leq r\mathbf 1\bigr].
\end{split}
\tag{3}
\]
After inserting (2) and the active-set representation of \(P_E\), (3) is a finite Boolean combination of linearly quantified affine systems.  Eliminate one scalar quantifier at a time: an existentially quantified scalar constrained by lower bounds, upper bounds, and equalities exists exactly when every induced lower bound is no larger than every induced upper bound and all induced equalities agree; a universal quantifier is eliminated by complementing the corresponding existential formula.  This finite Fourier--Motzkin elimination proves directly that the epigraph of \(f\), and likewise the strict epigraph obtained by replacing the terminal distance inequalities by strict ones, is semilinear.  Their boundary is the graph of the single-valued function \(f\).  Decomposing that graph into its finitely many relatively polyhedral cells gives a finite partition \(\{R_j\}_{j=1}^M\) of its domain such that
\[
 f(u,q)=a_j^{\mathsf T}u+b_j^{\mathsf T}q+c_j
 \quad\text{on }R_j.
\tag{4}
\]
Indeed, on any polyhedron contained in a single-valued graph, the last coordinate is an affine function of the projected coordinates; subdividing overlapping projections yields the asserted partition.  This is exactly the finite full-loss object compiled by the primal--dual elimination in the stated handle.  In particular, the compilation retains projection faces and both directions of Hausdorff excess, not only path-feasibility faces.

\emph{Step 2 (diagonal stratification and the homogeneous germ).}
Write the affine boundary forms of \(R_j\) as \(\ell_{jr}(u,q)\).  The normalized diagonal boundary forms and value-intercept forms are
\[
 \delta_{jr}(q)=\ell_{jr}(q,q),
 \qquad
 \eta_j(q)=(a_j+b_j)^{\mathsf T}q+c_j.
\tag{5}
\]
There are finitely many such forms.  Because \(q_\star\in Q_E\), projection fixes it and
\[
 f(q_\star,q_\star)=d_H\{S(q_\star),S(q_\star)\}=0.
\tag{6}
\]
The continuity-frontier theorem supplies \(H,\varepsilon>0\) such that
\[
 d_H\{S(r),S(q_\star)\}\leq H\|r-q_\star\|
 \quad\text{for }r\in\overline{\mathcal Q},\ \|r-q_\star\|<\varepsilon.
\tag{7}
\]
Euclidean projection is nonexpansive and \(P_Eq_\star=q_\star\).  The triangle inequality and (7) consequently give, whenever both arguments are sufficiently close to \(q_\star\),
\[
 0\leq f(u,q)
 \leq H\|P_Eu-q_\star\|+H\|q-q_\star\|
 \leq H\|u-q_\star\|+H\|q-q_\star\|.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus every cell of (4) incident to \((q_\star,q_\star)\) has zero affine value at that point, so its value-intercept form satisfies \(\eta_j(q_\star)=0\).

Restrict now to the sampling slice \((u,q)=(q_\star+v,q_\star)\) with \(v\in T=T_E(q_\star)\).  On an incident cell, (4)--(5) become
\[
 f(q_\star+v,q_\star)=a_j^{\mathsf T}v,
 \qquad
 \ell_{jr}(q_\star+v,q_\star)
   =\delta_{jr}(q_\star)+g_{jr}^{\mathsf T}v
\tag{9}
\]
for fixed vectors \(g_{jr}\).  Every nonzero number among the finite collection \(\{\delta_{jr}(q_\star),\eta_j(q_\star)\}\) is separated from zero.  Hence, in one neighborhood of the origin, its sign is fixed, while every zero boundary form in (9) is homogeneous in \(v\).  The reachable incident cells therefore cut \(T\) into finitely many polyhedral cones, and their linear values in (9) define a finite, nonnegative, positively homogeneous piecewise-linear map
\[
 \psi_{q_\star}:T\longrightarrow\mathbb R_+,
 \qquad
 f(q_\star+v,q_\star)=\psi_{q_\star}(v)
 \quad\text{for all sufficiently small }v\in T.
\tag{10}
\]
The map is continuous: (8) makes \(f\) continuous on this slice at the origin, and the affine formulas agree on every shared cell boundary because they represent the same single-valued function.  Conversely, every cone retained in (10) is the restriction of an incident cell of the exact graph (4).  Thus (10) contains all and only reachable zero-intercept pieces.

For completeness, define the diagonal stratum of \(q_\star\) by the signs, with zero retained as a separate sign, of every normalized form in (5).  On the relative interior of this stratum, nonzero forms keep their signs and zero forms remain zero; after translation by \(v\), the latter reduce to the same linear forms as in (9).  The incident cones and their slopes are therefore constant on that stratum.  This finite diagonal-stratum argument applies without alteration when several path images switch simultaneously or when \(p_0\), \(p_1\), and a policy threshold tie: duplicates may repeat cells, but cannot delete a cell of the exact graph.

\emph{Step 3 (exact recovery by snapping).}
Let one observation be represented by its \(4K\)-cell indicator vector \(W_i\), and let its mean be \(r_\star=(\pi_zq_{\star z})_{z=0,1}\).  Exact-face sampling implies that a structural-zero coordinate is zero almost surely and that every coordinate retained in the relative interior of \(E\) has positive probability.  For fixed \(t\), boundedness of \(W_i\) gives the characteristic-function expansion
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\!\left\{\frac{i t^{\mathsf T}(W_i-r_\star)}{\sqrt n}\right\}
 =1-\frac{t^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Var}(W_i)t}{2n}+o(n^{-1}).
\tag{11}
\]
Taking the \(n\)-th power yields the centered multivariate Gaussian limit for the joint cell shares.  Since \(\pi_z>0\),
\[
 \Pr(N_z=0)=(1-\pi_z)^n\longrightarrow0,
\tag{12}
\]
so conditional shares are well defined with probability tending to one.  Expanding the ratio of joint cell shares to the arm share gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat q_z-q_{\star z})
 =\frac{1}{\pi_z}
   (I-q_{\star z}\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T})
   \sqrt n(\widehat r_z-r_{\star z})+o_p(1).
\tag{13}
\]
Direct multiplication of the multinomial covariance in (13) gives zero cross-arm covariance and
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat q-q_\star)\Rightarrow G,
 \qquad
 \Sigma_z=\frac{\operatorname{diag}(q_{\star z})
                  -q_{\star z}q_{\star z}^{\mathsf T}}{\pi_z}
\tag{14}
\]
after deleting structural-zero and normalization directions.  On the resulting relative tangent space \(T\), \(\Sigma\) is positive definite: each retained cell probability is positive, and the only null direction of an arm's multinomial covariance is its normalization direction.  Thus (14) also proves \(\widehat q-q_\star=O_p(n^{-1/2})\).  Projection nonexpansiveness gives
\[
 \|\widetilde q-q_\star\|
 =\|P_E\widehat q-P_Eq_\star\|
 \leq\|\widehat q-q_\star\|
 =O_p(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{15}
\]

Let \(h\) be any normalized diagonal boundary or value-intercept form used by the handle.  From (15),
\[
 h(q_\star)=0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 |h(\widetilde q)|=O_p(n^{-1/2})=o_p(\kappa_n),
\tag{16}
\]
because \(\sqrt n\kappa_n\to\infty\).  If \(h(q_\star)\neq0\), consistency in (15) and \(\kappa_n\to0\) imply
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{|h(\widetilde q)|>\kappa_n,
       \ \operatorname{sgn}h(\widetilde q)=\operatorname{sgn}h(q_\star)\right\}
 \longrightarrow1.
\tag{17}
\]
The collection is finite, so (16)--(17) hold simultaneously with probability tending to one.  On that event, snapping reproduces exactly the diagonal stratum of \(q_\star\); the exact compilation from Step 1 and the stratum result from Step 2 then recover all and only the cones and slopes defining \(\psi_{q_\star}\).  Restriction to \(T\) removes every structural-zero sampling direction.  This proves recovery at ordinary cells, continuous multi-path switches, propensity--grid ties, and relative lower-dimensional exact faces in one argument.

\emph{Step 4 (limit law).}
Under exact-face sampling, \(\widehat q\in\operatorname{aff}(E)\) whenever both arm shares are nonzero.  On the event that \(\widehat q\) is in the neighborhood from (10), the definitions of \(f\) and \(\widetilde q\), followed by positive homogeneity, give the exact identity
\[
\begin{split}
 \sqrt n\,d_H\{S(\widetilde q),S(q_\star)\}
 &=\sqrt n\,f(\widehat q,q_\star)\\
 &=\psi_{q_\star}\!\left(\sqrt n(\widehat q-q_\star)\right).
\end{split}
\tag{18}
\]
The event has probability tending to one by (14).  Since \(\psi_{q_\star}\) is continuous, (14) and (18) imply
\[
 \sqrt n\,d_H\{S(\widetilde q),S(q_\star)\}
 \Rightarrow\psi_{q_\star}(G).
\tag{19}
\]
Notice that \(G\) is the unprojected first-stage limit: the directional effect of the possibly binding compatibility projection is already part of \(f\), hence of \(\psi_{q_\star}\).

\emph{Step 5 (conditional Gaussian calibration).}
On the same exact face, cell-share consistency and \(\pi_z>0\) make the plug-in version \(\widehat\Sigma\) of (14) consistent.  Couple a conditional Gaussian draw as \(\widehat G=\widehat\Sigma^{1/2}\xi\), where \(\xi\) is standard normal on \(T\) and independent of the data.  Continuity of the matrix square root, consistency of \(\widehat\Sigma\), and the probability-one germ recovery in Step 3 imply conditional convergence of
\[
 \widehat\psi_n(\widehat G)
 \quad\text{to the law of}\quad
 \psi_{q_\star}(G).
\tag{20}
\]
Let \(c_\star\) be the closed upper \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of the latter law and let \(\widehat c_n\) be its conditional simulated counterpart.  A positive atom is impossible away from zero.  Indeed, on each of finitely many cones, \(\psi_{q_\star}(g)=a^{\mathsf T}g\); for \(c>0\), the event \(a^{\mathsf T}G=c\) lies in a proper affine hyperplane and has probability zero because \(\Sigma\) is positive definite on \(T\).  If the map is not identically zero, scaling any point where it is positive also shows that its distribution function increases through every positive value in its range.  Therefore, when \(c_\star>0\), (20) gives \(\widehat c_n\to_p c_\star\), and (19) yields the desired limiting coverage.

If \(c_\star=0\), the zero set of the continuous piecewise-linear homogeneous map is a finite union of polyhedral cones whose boundary is contained in finitely many proper linear subspaces.  Hence it is a continuity set for the nondegenerate Gaussian law on \(T\), and (14), (18) give
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\sqrt n\,d_H\{S(\widetilde q),S(q_\star)\}=0\right\}
 \longrightarrow
 \Pr\{\psi_{q_\star}(G)=0\}\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{21}
\]
For any nonnegative guard \(\rho_n\downarrow0\), a closed ball with radius \((\widehat c_n+\rho_n)/\sqrt n\) contains the zero-loss event.  Combining the positive-quantile case with (21) proves
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_{q_\star}\!\left\{
 d_H\{S(\widetilde q),S(q_\star)\}
 \leq\frac{\widehat c_n+\rho_n}{\sqrt n}
 \right\}\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{22}
\]
The guard may also dominate a vanishing numerical quantile-computation error.

Finally, exact-face specification is load-bearing.  If the analyst declares a strict superface \(E'\supsetneq E\), then its tangent space decomposes as \(T_{E'}=T_E\oplus T_{\mathrm{extra}}\) with at least one direction in \(T_{\mathrm{extra}}\) that has identically zero empirical fluctuation under the true law.  Any compiled incident affine piece with nonzero slope on that direction is retained by the superface germ although its restriction to the true sampling experiment is absent.  Algebraically, the certificate is a retained coefficient \(a_j\) and \(e\in T_{\mathrm{extra}}\) with \(a_j^{\mathsf T}e\neq0\): the superface reports the values \(a_j^{\mathsf T}(v+se)\), while every feasible sample perturbation has \(s=0\).  Such coefficients occur whenever a structurally zero outcome cell enters a balance right-hand side \(B_\gamma q\) and changes a policy image under positive perturbation, which is permitted by (2).  Thus a strict superface can retain sampling-inaccessible loss pieces and can place a singular Gaussian law on their boundaries; Steps 3 and 5 no longer establish recovery of the true active stratum or its quantile.  This supplies the asserted failure certificate and proves why the theorem is pointwise on the certified exact face only.

prose_updates.tldr: A binary instrument identifies complier outcome distributions but policies below \(p_0\) and above \(p_1\) require extrapolation. Under exactly Marx's existential rank similarity and a fixed finite ordered outcome alphabet, the sharp simultaneous policy-mean set is a finite nonconvex union of common-rank path images, each attained by one law. This finite-alphabet missing-support class and Marx's full-support class are nonnested; the reduction to Marx applies only on their finite-alphabet full-support overlap, and the observable monotonicity inequalities are derived from the latent model. Path survival gives the exact Hausdorff continuity frontier and a centered local Lipschitz bound. A legal three-outcome contiguous submodel proves that globally honest metric procedures cannot shrink uniformly. A terminating finite algorithm computes the multinomial outer set, the set-of-sets image, and their exact Hausdorff radii; finite-sample coverage is the direct inversion corollary. On every certified continuity law, the full projected Hausdorff-loss germ is recovered pointwise on the exact multinomial sampling face, including continuous multi-path switches, propensity--grid ties, and exact lower-dimensional structural-zero faces; this requires positive instrument shares and does not imply globally shrinking honest metric inference.

project_justification.fill: The project derives the observable compatibility inequalities from the maintained latent model and supplies a sharp path-union representation, finite exclusion certificates, an if-and-only-if continuity frontier, a contiguous impossibility theorem, a terminating exact inversion-and-radius algorithm, the accompanying finite-sample coverage corollary, and pointwise projected full-loss Gaussian calibration at every certified continuity law on its exact multinomial sampling face. The calibration covers continuous multi-path switches, propensity--grid ties, and exact lower-dimensional structural-zero faces, requires positive instrument shares, and makes no uniform calibration or globally shrinking honest metric-inference claim. The finite-alphabet missing-support class and Marx's full-support class are nonnested, with the Marx reduction confined to their finite-alphabet full-support overlap.

prose_updates.related_work: Marx (2024) is the direct substantive anchor: Proposition 5 obtains uniformly sharp rank-similar policy bounds under full complier support, and footnote 29 identifies the construction that fails without it. The present finite-alphabet missing-support class and Marx's full-support class are nonnested; the reduction to Proposition 5 applies only on their finite-alphabet full-support overlap. Imbens and Rubin (1997) give the principal-stratum interpretation underlying the observable monotonicity inequalities; here those inequalities are derived as compatibility checks. Chesher (2010), Torgovitsky (2019), and Han and Yang (2024) show how discrete structural restrictions can be encoded by finite feasibility or linear programs; they inform the allocation representation but do not impose one common ordered rank across every latent-index bin. Beresteanu and Molinari (2008) and Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) provide regular Hausdorff theory for different set-valued substrates; the survival theorem addresses law-dependent component death in a nonconvex union. Romano and Shaikh (2010) motivate the coverage corollary through general identified-set inversion. Song et al. (2026) informs the finite categorical feasibility layer, while the algorithm theorem adds common-parameter nonconvex unions and exact outer-set and hyperspace Hausdorff radii. Fang and Santos (2019), Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), and Fan and Park (2010) motivate nonsmooth set-valued calibration; here the complete projected Hausdorff-loss germ is recovered pointwise at every certified continuity law on its exact multinomial sampling face, including continuous multi-path switches, propensity--grid ties, and exact lower-dimensional structural-zero faces, under positive instrument shares but without a uniform-calibration claim.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The projected full Hausdorff-loss germ is solved pointwise, including at continuous multi-path switches, propensity--grid ties, and exact lower-dimensional structural-zero sampling faces. The result remains conditional on a certified continuity law, positive instrument shares, and correct specification of the exact multinomial sampling face. It is not uniform over laws or faces, and a path-domain-only bootstrap still does not suffice because the full loss may change affine pieces while every path domain remains unchanged. None of these local calibration conclusions defeats the contiguous discontinuity obstruction to globally shrinking honest Hausdorff inference.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The path representation is scoped to a fixed finite outcome alphabet. That missing-support class and Marx's full-support class are nonnested, and the reduction to Marx's Proposition 5 holds only on their finite-alphabet full-support overlap. The inequalities \(c_0\ge0\) and \(c_1\ge0\) are derived observed-law compatibility checks, not maintained assumptions. The finite survival criterion, centered Lipschitz implication, three-outcome discontinuity, impossibility argument, and exact finite inversion-and-radius algorithm are theorem-level results. Simultaneous finite-sample coverage is a direct corollary of observed-law coverage and inversion, with no finite-sample optimality claim. Projected full-loss Gaussian calibration is solved pointwise at every certified continuity law on the exact multinomial sampling face, including continuous multi-path switches, propensity--grid ties, and exact lower-dimensional structural-zero faces; it requires positive instrument shares and the exact face. Pairwise-neighborhood Lipschitz continuity, a globally continuous derivative, uniform calibration, and globally shrinking honest Hausdorff inference are not claimed. The one-path folded-normal law is a check and special case of the general active-germ theorem. For \(K=2\), only the two monotone paths remain.
